summary: A server-rendered Java web app on Spring Boot with Thymeleaf pages, htmx partial updates and server-validated forms, built with Maven.
description: Write a Java web app that renders HTML on the server with Spring Boot, Spring MVC and Thymeleaf. One in-memory notes page proves the shape: a shared layout, an add form validated on the server that works with JavaScript off, htmx swapping in only the changed part of the page, CSRF tokens from Spring Security and one table behind every error page. Request ids, JSON access logs, validated settings and a health check come wired, and tests read the rendered HTML with MockMvc and a browser without JavaScript. The recipe picks no database, sign-in or hosting.
seoDescription: A Spring Boot web app recipe in Java: Thymeleaf templates, htmx, server-side form validation, CSRF, error pages, NullAway and HtmlUnit tests.

projectExamples.title: Internal admin console
projectExamples.description: Illustrative: replace notes with the records a back-office team edits through forms and lists. Sign-in, roles and a database are work the project still has to add.

plain.whatItIs: A starter website written in Java where the server builds each page, with forms that check what people type and show clear error pages.
goodAt: Internal tools and admin pages for teams that already run Java
Forms and lists that update in place without a JavaScript framework
Sites that must still work in browsers with JavaScript turned off
notGoodAt: Projects that need a database or sign-in from the start; you add both yourself.
Rich client-side interfaces; use a React or other single-page app stack for those.

requests: Spring Boot site with Thymeleaf templates and htmx
Java website that renders HTML on the server
server-side rendered Spring MVC pages without a JavaScript framework
Java form pages with validation, CSRF protection and error pages
replace an old JSP or Struts site with modern Spring Boot
caveats: Needs a JDK and Maven installed once to create the Maven wrapper; after that the wrapper downloads Maven itself.
The first build downloads every dependency and plugin, which takes a few minutes.
